spec.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa Square
spec.description: Jemaa el-Fnaa is the historic main square of Marrakech and one of the city's most important public spaces. Located at the heart of the medina, it has served for centuries as a meeting place, marketplace and stage for public life. During the day, the square hosts merchants, juice stalls and traditional activities, while in the evening it transforms into a lively open-air gathering place filled with food stalls, musicians, performers and storytellers. Jemaa el-Fnaa is especially significant for its living traditions and oral culture, which contributed to its international recognition as intangible cultural heritage.

access.comment: The square is a public space and can be accessed freely. The atmosphere changes throughout the day, with food stalls and traditional performances becoming especially active in the late afternoon and evening.

timeline.title: Origins of Marrakech
timeline.description: Marrakech was founded during the Almoravid period. An important open space developed near the city's early palace and market areas, forming the historical origins of the square.

timeline.title: Almohad period
timeline.description: Following the Almohad conquest of Marrakech, the surrounding urban landscape changed significantly, but the large public space continued to serve the city.

timeline.title: Jemaa el-Fnaa name appears in historical records
timeline.description: Historical sources from around the Saadian period record the name associated with Jemaa el-Fnaa. The precise origin and meaning of the name remain debated.

timeline.title: Protected cultural space
timeline.description: Measures were introduced to protect Jemaa el-Fnaa and preserve its distinctive cultural and artistic character.

timeline.title: UNESCO recognition
timeline.description: UNESCO proclaimed the cultural space of Jemaa el-Fnaa as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.

timeline.title: Intangible Cultural Heritage
timeline.description: The cultural space of Jemaa el-Fnaa was incorporated into UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
